summary: After upgrading to 2.6, existing controller OAuth applications keep working and can be edited but not created, and controller personal access tokens are deprecated; move to platform OAuth applications and gateway tokens. From 2.4, all authenticator configs including SAML keys and OAuth secrets migrate automatically except custom LDAP certificates; from 2.5, LDAP and other authenticator settings are left as they were.
questions: Do my controller OAuth tokens work after upgrading to AAP 2.6?
Are controller personal access tokens deprecated in 2.6?
Do I need to migrate LDAP certificates manually when upgrading?
Can I still create controller OAuth applications in 2.6?

answer_card.title: Tokens and OAuth apps after upgrading to 2.6
answer_card.answer_md:
- **Controller OAuth applications:** still work and can be viewed and edited, but not created. Plan to move to **platform OAuth applications**.
- **Controller personal access tokens:** deprecated. Move to **platform gateway tokens**.
- **Authenticators from 2.4:** migrated automatically, including SAML private keys and OAuth secrets. **Custom LDAP certificates must be migrated manually.**
- **Authenticators from 2.5:** not re-imported; they keep working as they are.
